issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff cannot exclude the time spent prosecuting an earlier proceeding from the limitation period when the plaintiff deliberately proceeds despite an early objection that a necessary party is absent and chooses to bear the risk of that omission.
material_facts: The later suit was filed more than twelve years after the relevant revenue sales, so it depended on excluding the time spent in the earlier suit and appeal to be within limitation.
The earlier suit concerned the same cause of action but was ultimately dismissed because the Government was a necessary party and had not been impleaded.
The defendants objected to the omission of the Government at an early stage.
The plaintiff resisted the objection and, during revision proceedings, expressly chose to proceed without adding the Government, accepting the risk of that choice.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff did not prosecute the earlier proceeding in good faith, so its duration could not be excluded from the limitation period; the later suit was barred by limitation and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14 of the Limitation Act, 1908 permits exclusion of time spent prosecuting another civil proceeding, with due diligence and in good faith, against the defendant, on the same cause of action, in a court unable to entertain it because of a defect of jurisdiction or other cause of a like nature. Under Section 2(7), an act is not done in good faith unless it is done with due care and attention. The deliberate choice to continue despite an early objection to non-joinder, rather than correct the defect, was not a case of ignorance of law or a bona fide mistake on a doubtful point. Bishambhur Haldar v. Bonomali Haldar, ILR 26 Calcutta 414, was distinguished as involving a mistake of law on a doubtful point.

rule.if: civil_suit_with_limitation_claim and earlier_same_cause_proceeding and necessary_party_omitted and objection_raised_early and plaintiff_refused_to_add_party and plaintiff_chose_to_proceed_at_risk and later_suit_filed_after_limitation_period

predicates.civil_suit_with_limitation_claim: A party brought a civil suit whose timeliness depended on whether time spent in an earlier proceeding could be excluded.
predicates.earlier_same_cause_proceeding: The party previously prosecuted a civil proceeding against the opposing party on the same cause of action.
predicates.necessary_party_omitted: A party necessary to the earlier suit was not joined in that proceeding.
predicates.objection_raised_early: The opposing party objected to the missing necessary party at an early stage of the earlier proceeding.
predicates.plaintiff_refused_to_add_party: The plaintiff resisted the objection and did not add the necessary party to the earlier proceeding.
predicates.plaintiff_chose_to_proceed_at_risk: The plaintiff expressly chose to continue the earlier proceeding while accepting the risk of proceeding without the necessary party.
predicates.later_suit_filed_after_limitation_period: The later suit was filed after the applicable limitation period measured without excluding time spent in the earlier proceeding.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff brings a civil suit after the limitation period and the earlier same-cause proceeding continued despite an early objection to an omitted necessary party that the plaintiff chose not to add, the later suit is barred by limitation.
